answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity bond that burns on proven fraud. To register, an agent must forge a valid puzzle and lock a stake tied to a short-lived comet of reputation, while every new alias starts at zero and needs its own on-chain identity. Running N identities costs N times the capital and N times the compute, and since reputation is archived like marble it cannot be shuttled between aliases, so one convincing fake already costs real money.
